question: Does my dog need a licence, and how do I get one?

nuggets.text: A dog four months or older must be licensed.
nuggets.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person other than a releasing agency that has registered as such annually with local animal control to own a dog four months old or older in the Commonwealth unless such dog is licensed, as required by the provisions of this article.

nuggets.text: The tax is at most $10 a year or $50 for a lifetime licence.
nuggets.quote: The tax for each dog or cat shall not be more than $10 for each year or $50 for a lifetime license issued pursuant to subsection B of § 3.2-6530 .

nuggets.text: The licence is obtained within 30 days of the dog reaching four months or being acquired.
nuggets.quote: The license tax as prescribed in § 3.2-6528 is due not later than 30 days after a dog or cat has reached the age of four months, or not later than 30 days after an owner acquires a dog or cat four months of age or older, and each year thereafter.

nuggets.text: The application needs a current rabies vaccination certificate.
nuggets.quote: satisfactory evidence that such dog or cat has been inoculated or vaccinated against rabies by a currently licensed veterinarian or currently licensed veterinary technician who was under the immediate and direct supervision of a licensed veterinarian on the premises.

nuggets.text: In Charlottesville the City Treasurer sells the licence.
The city's lifetime dog licence costs $10.
nuggets.quote: Download the application (PDF, fillable). It asks for the owner's name, address and phone number, and for each dog its name and rabies expiration date, at $10 per dog. Attach a copy of the current rabies certificate, or ask your veterinarian to send the Treasurer's Office a copy.
